The first release of AutoVolumeControl on GitHub 🎉

AutoVolumeControl is a small Windows tray app that keeps the volume and mute state of your apps in sync with the
master volume of the default playback device.

## Why you might need it

On some audio devices the Windows master volume has no effect on certain outputs. The classic case is the **digital
(optical / S/PDIF) output of Creative Sound Blaster devices** such as the Sound BlasterX G6: the Windows volume bar,
the volume keys on your keyboard and even the knob on the device do nothing. Only the per-app volumes in the Windows
volume mixer still work there.

AutoVolumeControl applies the master volume to every running app, so the volume bar, your keyboard and the knob on
the device work again, and so does mute.

## Features

- 🔊 **Master volume and mute follow through to your apps.** Volume keys, the Windows volume bar and the device knob
  work on outputs that otherwise ignore them.
- ✅ **Choose which apps are synced.** Right-click the tray icon. New apps are synced by default as soon as they
  start playing audio.
- 🎚️ **Per-app ratio.** A slider per app sets its volume as a share of the master volume, e.g. music always at 60 %
  of whatever the master is set to. The mouse wheel moves it in 5 % steps.
- 🏷️ **Recognizable entries.** Each app is shown with its icon and window title, e.g. "Artist - Song" for Spotify or
  the active tab for a browser.
- 🔁 **Robust.** Follows changes of the default playback device, reacts immediately when apps start, stop or change
  their own volume, and recovers by itself when the Windows audio service restarts. Apps that keep resetting their
  volume are throttled instead of fought in a loop.
- 🔍 **App Scale.** Show the menu at 85 %, 100 %, 115 % or 130 % of its normal size, on top of the Windows display
  scaling. It stays sharp on high-DPI displays.
- 🚀 **Start with Windows** (optional).
- 📦 **One portable exe.** No installer and no admin rights needed. Settings are stored per user in the registry.

## New since 1.4

Per-app volume ratios, app icons and window titles, App Scale, automatic recovery from audio service restarts, a
sharp menu on high-DPI displays, a single-instance guard, a diagnostics log and many fixes. See the full
[changelog](https://github.com/SesioN/AutoVolumeControl/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md).

## Installation

1. Download `AutoVolumeControl.exe` below.
2. Put it in a permanent location, e.g. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\AutoVolumeControl\`, and start it.
3. Right-click the tray icon to choose the apps and turn on **Start with Windows** if you like.

Requires Windows 10 or 11 with .NET Framework 4.8 (included since Windows 10 version 1903).

**Upgrading from an older version:** exit the old version and replace its exe. Your app selection is kept. If the
new exe is in a different location, turn **Start with Windows** on again so it points to the new file.

The exe is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on the first start (**More info → Run anyway**). It is
built from this tag by [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/SesioN/AutoVolumeControl/actions/workflows/build.yml); you
can verify your download with the checksum below (`Get-FileHash AutoVolumeControl.exe` in PowerShell).
